conventions: Royal filiation formula. In `X בֶּן־Y מֶלֶךְ Z` → *X the son of Y king of Z*, the construct בֵּן takes a supplied *the* under rule 29 and the apposed construct מֶלֶךְ is written bare, taking no supplied determiner, because the ASV writes one *the* for the phrase and it stands before *son*. So 2CH.22.1, 22.5, 22.6 (twice) and 22.7. Where an article morpheme stands in such a chain instead, the fronting sentences of rule 29 govern and the construct is the bare one — 22.11's `בַּת־הַמֶּלֶךְ יְהוֹרָם` → *the daughter of king Jehoram*.

The determiner count of rule 29 is run phrase by phrase, and one verse may contain both shapes. 2CH.22.11 writes `בַּת־הַמֶּלֶךְ` → *the daughter of the king*, where the rectum is arthrous, nothing is fronted, the article takes the *the* before its own word and the construct takes a supplied one; and `בַּת־הַמֶּלֶךְ יְהוֹרָם` → *the daughter of king Jehoram*, where the rectum is anarthrous, the phrase's single written *the* is the article's fronted to the left edge, and the construct keeps only *daughter*. 22.10 (`זֶרַע הַמַּמְלָכָה` → *the seed royal*) and 22.12 (`בֵית הָאֱלֹהִים` → *the house of God*) are the fronting shape as well. Read which determiner stands before the rectum's own word; do not read the left edge as evidence of fronting, and do not mark a present article unrepresented while a supplied *the* holds the written word.

2CH.22.6 s007: the ASV's *of the wounds* answers to the מִן of the parallel at 2 Kings 8:29, where the projection carries כִּי, and the packet records no variant unit in that slot. Under rule 53's closing paragraph the printed English is aligned against the token that is there, so the כִּי holds the *of* and the divergence is named in the unit's note. Do not renormalize this to an unrepresented conjunction beside a supplied preposition on `הַמַּכִּים`: rule 9 forbids taking a textual decision here, and the ASV margin (*The text has because the wounds which etc.*) corroborates the divergence without deciding it, by rule 38.
report: Read all twelve verses end to end against the 36-lemma candidate table and found no genuine cross-verse split: every candidate group is one construction whose difference the source or the ASV's own wording licenses.

גַּם + הָלַךְ: 22.3 writes an explicit הוּא, which takes *He* while the verb keeps *walked*; 22.5 writes no pronoun, so the verb takes *He walked* under rule 17. חָבָא goes the same way — 22.9 has no finite verb and the participle takes the construction-supplied copula, 22.12 writes וַיְהִי, which takes it.

Infinitive-construct clauses divide identically throughout: the preposition takes the *when*, *to* or *in that*, the infinitive keeps the verb, and the subject pronoun goes to a suffix where one stands (22.2, 22.6, 22.7 s013) and to the infinitive itself where none does (22.7 s008, rules 48 and 52).

מִן before a construct noun: 22.11 splits מִתּוֹךְ → *from among* and fuses מִפְּנֵי → *from*. That is rule 30's one-rendering condition counted correctly in both directions inside one verse, not two analyses; rule 30 names both shapes itself.

בֵּית reads one way everywhere: a supplied *the* on the construct where no article morpheme stands (22.3, 22.4, 22.7, 22.8, 22.9, 22.10), and the article's own written *the*, fronted, where one does (22.12). The בֵּן/מֶלֶךְ filiation formula likewise: supplied *the* on בֵּן, apposed מֶלֶךְ bare, in 22.1, 22.5, 22.6 twice and 22.7.

Zero `added` units is correct here, which the lemma table could not have shown. The three supplied runs that could have been marked are each licensed by a morpheme standing in the clause: *of men* on גְּדוּד (rule 31's supplied generic with its own *of*), the second *did* on עָשָׂה (rule 34's pro-verb, the Hebrew writing that verb once in the coordination), and *away* on גָּנַב (rule 44, the removal being written in the clause by מִתּוֹךְ).

BSB: none of the eight disagreements is an error, and every one is the documented convention split. 22.1 הַ is rule 41's limit, the phrase's single determiner being the possessive the suffix licenses; the four לְ tokens in 22.4 and 22.9 are rule 40 recastings, three datives rewritten as possessive determiners and one whose object the ASV promotes to English subject; 22.7 וֹ is rule 22's resumptive, the ASV writing one *whom* for two morphemes pointing at the antecedent; 22.10 וַ is the apodosis connective left bare after *Now when*; 22.11 אֹת is an ordinary object marker. Nothing was changed to move the rate.

Nothing to promote. The two constructions that looked novel are already written: חֲדַר הַמִּטּוֹת → *bedchamber* is rule 30's דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים → *chronicles* fusion with the article separately taking the written *the*, headed by rule 23's tie sentence; and the 22.6 כִּי → *of* is rule 53's closing paragraph in its own terms. Three conventions recorded instead.
